def download(
    self, name: str, output_path: Path | str | None = None, timeout: float = 60
) -> Path:
    """Download a model package from the drone as a zip.

    Args:
        name: The package's directory slug.
        output_path: Destination file or directory. Defaults to the filename the
            drone suggests (or `<name>.zip`) in the current directory.
        timeout: Request timeout in seconds.

    Returns:
        The path the zip was written to.
    """
    response = self._check(requests.get(f"{self._base_url}/{name}/download", timeout=timeout))
    disposition = response.headers.get("Content-Disposition", "")
    matches = re.findall('filename="([^"]+)"', disposition)
    filename = matches[0] if matches else f"{name}.zip"

    if output_path is None:
        output_path = Path(filename)
    else:
        output_path = Path(output_path)
        if output_path.is_dir():
            output_path = output_path / filename
    output_path.write_bytes(response.content)
    return output_path

def list(self, timeout: float = 5) -> list[CvModel]:
    """List the model packages installed on the drone.

    Args:
        timeout: Request timeout in seconds.

    Returns:
        One CvModel per installed package, sorted by directory name.
    """
    response = self._check(requests.get(f"{self._base_url}/", timeout=timeout))
    models = [CvModel.from_json(entry) for entry in response.json()]
    return sorted(models, key=lambda model: model.directory)

rescan(timeout: float | None = None) -> None

Ask the drone's vision pipeline to rescan the installed packages.

The request is the RescanCvModelsCtrl control message, so the drone has to be connected; an observer connection is enough. The drone has no file watcher, so a package uploaded, deleted or reconfigured stays as it was until a rescan or a reboot. upload, delete and the set_* methods send one themselves while connected, so this is for changes made some other way. A rescan restarts every running model, and models only run while a client in control pets the watchdog.

    Ignored. The rescan used to be an HTTP request with a timeout; the argument stays so code written for 2.8.0 keeps working.

def rescan(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
    """Ask the drone's vision pipeline to rescan the installed packages.

    The request is the `RescanCvModelsCtrl` control message, so the drone has to be
    connected; an observer connection is enough. The drone has no file watcher, so a
    package uploaded, deleted or reconfigured stays as it was until a rescan or a reboot.
    [`upload`][blueye.sdk.cv_models.CvModels.upload],
    [`delete`][blueye.sdk.cv_models.CvModels.delete] and the `set_*` methods send one
    themselves while connected, so this is for changes made some other way. A rescan
    restarts every running model, and models only run while a client in control pets the
    watchdog.

    Args:
        timeout: Ignored. The rescan used to be an HTTP request with a timeout; the
            argument stays so code written for 2.8.0 keeps working.

    Raises:
        ConnectionError: If the drone is not connected.
    """
    if timeout is not None:
        warnings.warn(
            "`CvModels.rescan` sends a control message and no longer takes a timeout, "
            "the argument is ignored and will be removed in the next major version",
            DeprecationWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    self._parent_drone._ctrl_client.rescan_cv_models()

Upload a model package zip to the drone.

The drone validates the archive (it must contain a valid model_meta.json and the model file it references) and installs it into a directory named after the slugified model name — an existing package with the same slug is replaced.

Parameters:

    The installed model as reported by the drone.

def upload(self, package: Path | str, timeout: float = 60) -> CvModel:
    """Upload a model package zip to the drone.

    The drone validates the archive (it must contain a valid model_meta.json and
    the model file it references) and installs it into a directory named after
    the slugified model name — an existing package with the same slug is
    replaced.

    Args:
        package: Path to the package zip (e.g. produced by
            `blueye bundle-model`).
        timeout: Request timeout in seconds; model files can be large.

    Returns:
        The installed model as reported by the drone.
    """
    package = Path(package)
    with package.open("rb") as file_handle:
        response = requests.post(
            f"{self._base_url}/upload", files={"file": file_handle}, timeout=timeout
        )
    model = CvModel.from_json(self._check(response).json())
    self._request_rescan()
    return model

set_water_density(density: float)

Set the water density the drone uses to convert pressure to depth.

The drone starts with salt water, 1025 grams per liter. The Blueye app sends the salinity chosen by the pilot each time it takes control, so a value set here lasts until the app or another client sends a new one. The drone rescales its current depth reading when the density changes.

The WaterDensities class contains typical densities for salty-, brackish-, and fresh water (these are the same values that the Blueye app uses).

def set_water_density(self, density: float):
    """Set the water density the drone uses to convert pressure to depth.

    The drone starts with salt water, 1025 grams per liter. The Blueye app sends the salinity
    chosen by the pilot each time it takes control, so a value set here lasts until the app
    or another client sends a new one. The drone rescales its current depth reading when the
    density changes.

    The [WaterDensities][blueye.sdk.constants.WaterDensities] class contains typical densities
    for salty-, brackish-, and fresh water (these are the same values that the Blueye app uses).

    Args:
        density (float): The water density in grams per liter.
    """
    self._parent_drone._ctrl_client.set_water_density(density)
    self._water_density = density

def __init__(
    self,
    ip="192.168.1.101",
    auto_connect=True,
    timeout=10,
    disconnect_other_clients=False,
    connect_as_observer=False,
    **connect_args: Dict[str, Any],
):
    """Initialize the Drone class.

    Args:
        ip (str, optional):
            The IP address of the drone.
        auto_connect (bool, optional):
            Whether to automatically connect to the drone.
        timeout (int, optional):
            The timeout for the connection attempt.
        disconnect_other_clients (bool, optional):
            Whether to disconnect other clients.
        connect_as_observer (bool, optional):
            Whether to connect as an observer.
        **connect_args:
            Additional keyword arguments to pass to the [`connect`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.connect]
            method.
    """
    self._ip = ip
    self.camera = Camera(self, is_guestport_camera=False)
    """The main camera: recording, pictures and camera parameters.

    See [`Camera`][blueye.sdk.camera.Camera]. Camera tilt is under `camera.tilt`
    ([`Tilt`][blueye.sdk.camera.Tilt]) and the video overlay under `camera.overlay`
    ([`Overlay`][blueye.sdk.camera.Overlay])."""
    self.motion = Motion(self)
    """Thruster input and the auto modes, see [`Motion`][blueye.sdk.motion.Motion]."""
    self.logs = Logs(self)
    """The dive logs stored on the drone, see [`Logs`][blueye.sdk.logs.Logs]."""
    self.legacy_logs = LegacyLogs(self)
    """Logs in the CSV format of Blunux versions before 3.0.

    See [`LegacyLogs`][blueye.sdk.logs.LegacyLogs]."""
    self.config = Config(self)
    """Drone time and water density, see [`Config`][blueye.sdk.drone.Config]."""
    self.battery = Battery(self)
    """Battery state, see [`Battery`][blueye.sdk.battery.Battery]."""
    self.telemetry = Telemetry(self)
    """Telemetry messages, callbacks and publish rates.

    See [`Telemetry`][blueye.sdk.drone.Telemetry]."""
    self.mission = Mission(self)
    """Loading and running missions, see [`Mission`][blueye.sdk.mission.Mission]."""
    self.cv_models = CvModels(self)
    """Computer vision models installed on the drone.

    See [`CvModels`][blueye.sdk.cv_models.CvModels]."""
    self.connected = False
    """Whether the drone is connected.

    True between a successful [`connect`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.connect] and
    [`disconnect`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.disconnect]."""
    self.client_id: int = None
    """The id the drone assigned to this client when connecting, `None` before that."""
    self.in_control: bool = False
    """Whether this client held control when it connected or last took control.

    Set by [`connect`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.connect] and
    [`take_control`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.take_control]. Not updated when the drone hands
    control to another client; compare
    [`get_client_in_control`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.get_client_in_control] with
    `client_id` for the current state."""
    # Set by connect() from the drone's HTTP drone_info. Declared here, without a value, so
    # the reference documents them; reading one before connecting raises AttributeError.
    self.features: List[str]
    """Optional hardware the drone reported when connecting, as a list of names.

    `"tilt"` on every model except the original Pioneer, `"gpdrone"` on drones with guest
    ports, and `"gplight"`, `"gpcam"` and `"gripper"` when such a device is attached. The
    [`Tilt`][blueye.sdk.camera.Tilt] methods raise `RuntimeError` without `"tilt"`. Not
    updated while connected. Empty when the drone could not read its hardware within its own
    5 s limit and answered with default information instead. Use
    [`peripherals`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.peripherals] for the attached devices."""
    self.software_version: str
    """The full Blunux version string, such as `"5.2.212-wrynose-jetson-dev"`.

    Set when connecting."""
    self.software_version_short: str
    """The Blunux version number without the build suffix, such as `"5.2.212"`.

    Set when connecting."""
    self.serial_number: str
    """The drone's serial number. Set when connecting."""
    self.uuid: str
    """The drone's hardware id. Set when connecting."""
    # The drone's persistent storage settings from drone_info, which say which media the
    # drone writes at all. None until read, and on drones that do not report them.
    self._storage_settings: Optional[Dict[str, bool]] = None
    self._watchdog_publisher = _NoConnectionClient()
    self._telemetry_watcher = _NoConnectionClient()
    self._req_rep_client = _NoConnectionClient()
    self._ctrl_client = _NoConnectionClient()

    self.peripherals: Optional[List[Peripheral]] = None
    """The peripherals connected to the drone's guest ports.

    `None` until the drone has reported its guest ports (through `DroneInfoTel`), and an
    empty list when the drone reports no peripherals.

    The drone can report its guest ports after `connect()` returns, so the shortcuts below
    can still be `None` right after connecting. While `peripherals` is `None`, a `None`
    shortcut means "not reported yet" rather than "not attached". Every shortcut is `None`
    again after `disconnect()`."""
    self._guest_ports: Optional[List[GuestPort]] = None
    self.external_camera: Optional[GuestPortCamera] = None
    """Camera on a guest port, or `None` if none has been discovered.

    See [`peripherals`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.peripherals]."""
    self.external_light: Optional[GuestPortLight] = None
    """Light on a guest port, or `None` if none has been discovered.

    See [`peripherals`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.peripherals]."""
    self.gripper: Optional[Gripper] = None
    """Gripper on a guest port, or `None` if none has been discovered.

    See [`peripherals`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.peripherals]."""
    self.laser: Optional[Laser] = None
    """Scaling laser on a guest port, or `None` if none has been discovered.

    See [`peripherals`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.peripherals]."""
    self.servo: Optional[GenericServo] = None
    """Generic servo on a guest port, or `None` if none has been discovered.

    See [`peripherals`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.peripherals]."""
    self.skid_servo: Optional[SkidServo] = None
    """Multibeam (skid) servo on a guest port, or `None` if none has been discovered.

    See [`peripherals`][blueye.sdk.drone.Drone.peripherals]."""
    self._guest_ports_known = False
    self._drone_info_cb_id: Optional[str] = None
    # The drone publishes one GenericServoTel per guest port under the same message type, so
    # the telemetry store only keeps the last one. This keeps the latest per port, filled by
    # a callback that is registered while a generic servo is discovered.
    self._generic_servo_tel: Dict[
        blueye.protocol.GuestPortNumber, blueye.protocol.GenericServoTel
    ] = {}
    self._generic_servo_cb_id: Optional[str] = None

    if auto_connect is True:
        self.connect(
            timeout=timeout,
            disconnect_other_clients=disconnect_other_clients,
            connect_as_observer=connect_as_observer,
            **connect_args,
        )

Spawns several threads for receiving telemetry, sending control messages, and publishing watchdog messages.

A watchdog message from the client in control arms the thrusters. When this connection receives control during setup, the SDK zeroes the thruster setpoints and synchronizes the drone's clock. An observer connection does neither and is excluded from control handover. Observer mode does not prevent setters from sending commands.

    Information about the client connecting. If None, the SDK supplies its version and uses Python's platform module for the OS and hostname shown in the app.

  • timeout (float, default: 4 ) –

    Seconds to wait for connection.

  • disconnect_other_clients (bool, default: False ) –

    If True, disconnect clients until the drone reports that we are in control.

  • connect_as_observer (bool, default: False ) –

    If the connection attempt fails.

  • RuntimeError –

    If the Blunux version of the connected drone is too old.

def connect(
    self,
    client_info: blueye.protocol.ClientInfo = None,
    timeout: float = 4,
    disconnect_other_clients: bool = False,
    connect_as_observer: bool = False,
    log_notifications: bool = False,
):
    """Establish a connection to the drone.

    Spawns several threads for receiving telemetry, sending control messages, and publishing
    watchdog messages.

    A watchdog message from the client in control arms the thrusters. When this connection
    receives control during setup, the SDK zeroes the thruster setpoints and synchronizes the
    drone's clock. An observer connection does neither and is excluded from control handover.
    Observer mode does not prevent setters from sending commands.

    Args:
        client_info (blueye.protocol.ClientInfo, optional):
            Information about the client connecting. If None, the SDK supplies its version
            and uses Python's `platform` module for the OS and hostname shown in the app.
        timeout (float, optional):
            Seconds to wait for connection.
        disconnect_other_clients (bool, optional):
            If True, disconnect clients until the drone reports that we are in control.
        connect_as_observer (bool, optional):
            If True, the client will not be promoted to in control of the drone.
        log_notifications (bool, optional):
            If True, the notifications will be logged using the logging module.

    Raises:
        ConnectionError: If the connection attempt fails.
        RuntimeError: If the Blunux version of the connected drone is too old.
    """
    logger.info(f"Attempting to connect to drone at {self._ip}")
    time_connection_start = time.time()
    self._update_drone_info(timeout=timeout)
    self._verify_required_blunux_version("3.2")

    self._telemetry_watcher = TelemetryClient(self)
    self._ctrl_client = CtrlClient(self)
    self._watchdog_publisher = WatchdogPublisher(self)
    self._req_rep_client = ReqRepClient(self)

    self._telemetry_watcher.start()
    self._req_rep_client.start()
    self._ctrl_client.start()

    # Anything that fails from here on must not leave the threads behind. A watchdog thread
    # that outlives a failed connect() would pet the drone as client 0, which the drone takes
    # as the client in control whenever nobody is, and that keeps its failsafe from tripping.
    try:
        self._connect(
            client_info, disconnect_other_clients, connect_as_observer, log_notifications
        )
    except BaseException:
        self._stop_clients()
        raise
    logger.debug("Connected in {:.2f} seconds".format(time.time() - time_connection_start))

docs.title: disconnect
docs.text:
disconnect(timeout: float = 1.0)

Disconnects the connection, allowing another client to take control of the drone.

The drone keeps the last motion input it received until a new one arrives or its watchdog times out, and on a handover to another client the watchdog never times out. So when this client is in control, every setpoint is zeroed and sent before the drone is told that the client is leaving.

Does nothing when there is no connection, such as after a failed connect(), so it is safe in a finally block.

Parameters:

  • timeout (float, default: 1.0 ) –

    Seconds to wait for the zero setpoint and any other queued control message to go out before the disconnect request is sent.

Source code in blueye/sdk/drone.py 
def disconnect(self, timeout: float = 1.0):
    """Disconnects the connection, allowing another client to take control of the drone.

    The drone keeps the last motion input it received until a new one arrives or its
    watchdog times out, and on a handover to another client the watchdog never times out.
    So when this client is in control, every setpoint is zeroed and sent before the drone is
    told that the client is leaving.

    Does nothing when there is no connection, such as after a failed `connect()`, so it is
    safe in a `finally` block.

    Args:
        timeout (float, optional): Seconds to wait for the zero setpoint and any other
            queued control message to go out before the disconnect request is sent.
    """
    if isinstance(self._req_rep_client, _NoConnectionClient):
        # Never connected, already disconnected, or connect() failed and stopped the threads
        return
    if self.connected:
        # No motion input from other threads or callbacks after this, so that the zero is
        # the last input the drone gets from this client
        in_control = self._has_control_now()
        self.motion._stop_input(zero=in_control)
        if in_control and not self._ctrl_client.flush(timeout):
            logger.warning("The zero thruster setpoint did not go out before disconnecting")
    self.connected = False
    _connected_drones.discard(self)
    try:
        self._req_rep_client.disconnect_client(self.client_id)
    except blueye.protocol.exceptions.ResponseTimeout:
        # If there's no response the connection is likely already closed, so we can just
        # continue to stop threads and disconnect
        pass
    self._stop_clients()

def get_attitude(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, float]]:
    """Get the current orientation of the drone as signed angles.

    Unlike `get_pose`, the angles are returned as the drone reports them: 0 when the drone is
    level and pointing north, with small deviations keeping their sign. A roll to the right and

def get_error_flags(self) -> Dict[str, bool]:
    """Get the error flags.

    Returns:
        The error flags as bools in a dictionary.
    """
    error_flags_tel = self.telemetry.get(blueye.protocol.ErrorFlagsTel)
    if error_flags_tel is None:
        return None
    error_flags_msg = error_flags_tel.error_flags
    error_flags = {}
    possible_flags = [attr for attr in dir(error_flags_msg) if not attr.startswith("__")]
    for flag in possible_flags:
        error_flags[flag] = getattr(error_flags_msg, flag)
    return error_flags

def get_pose(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, float]]:
    """Get the current orientation of the drone.

    The angles are wrapped to 0..359, so a drone rolled slightly to the left reports a roll
    just below 360. Use `get_attitude` for signed angles.

    Returns:
        A dictionary with roll, pitch, and yaw in degrees, from 0 to 359. None if no attitude
        telemetry has been received.
    """
    attitude_tel = self.telemetry.get(blueye.protocol.AttitudeTel)
    if attitude_tel is None:
        return None
    attitude = attitude_tel.attitude
    pose = {
        "roll": (attitude.roll + 360) % 360,
        "pitch": (attitude.pitch + 360) % 360,
        "yaw": (attitude.yaw + 360) % 360,
    }
    return pose

def take_control(self, timeout=1):
    """Take control of the drone, disconnecting other clients.

    Will disconnect other clients until the client is in control of the drone.

    Args:
        timeout (int, optional): The timeout for taking control.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the client could not take control of the drone in the given time.
    """
    start_time = time.time()
    client_in_control = self.get_client_in_control()
    while self.client_id != client_in_control:
        if time.time() - start_time > timeout:
            raise RuntimeError("Could not take control of the drone in the given time")
        resp = self._req_rep_client.disconnect_client(client_in_control)
        client_in_control = resp.client_id_in_control
    self.in_control = True

    The callback is called each time a message of the type is received.

        msg_filter (List[proto.message.Message]):

def get(
    self, msg_type: proto.message.Message, deserialize=True
) -> Optional[proto.message.Message | bytes]:
    """Get the latest telemetry message of the specified type.

    Args:
        msg_type (proto.message.Message):
            The message type to get. E.g., blueye.protocol.DepthTel.
        deserialize (bool, optional):
            If True, the message will be deserialized before being returned. If False, the raw
            bytes will be returned.

    Returns:
        The latest message of the specified type, or None if no message has been received yet.
    """
    try:
        msg = self._parent_drone._telemetry_watcher.get(msg_type)
    except KeyError:
        if version.parse(self._parent_drone.software_version_short) >= version.parse("3.3"):
            msg = self._parent_drone._req_rep_client.get_telemetry_msg(msg_type).payload.value
            if msg == b"":
                return None
        else:
            return None
    if deserialize:
        return msg_type.deserialize(msg)
    else:
        return msg

set_msg_log_frequency(msg: Message, frequency: float)

Set how often a specific telemetry message is written to the dive log.

The log frequency is independent of the publish frequency, so a message can be logged at a higher rate than it is published to clients, or the other way around. Like the publish frequency it is shared by every client and stays in effect until the drone reboots, with one exception: on the X3 Ultra and X7 a multibeam recording raises the log rate of PositionEstimateTel, AttitudeTel, CalibratedImuTel, CalibratedImuHpTel, DepthTel and AltitudeTel while it runs and restores their defaults when it stops, which replaces a rate set here for those six.

Parameters:

  • msg (Message) –

    The message to set the log frequency of. Needs to be one of the messages in blueye.protocol that end in Tel, e.g., blueye.protocol.Imu1Tel.

  • frequency (float) –

    The frequency in Hz. Must be greater than 0 and at most 100.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the frequency is not greater than 0 and at most 100 Hz.

  • RuntimeError –

    If the connected drone is running a Blunux version older than 5.1.0, or if the drone refuses to change the log frequency, because the connected drone does not publish the message or logs it as its data arrives rather than on a timer.

def set_msg_log_frequency(self, msg: proto.message.Message, frequency: float):
    """Set how often a specific telemetry message is written to the dive log.

    The log frequency is independent of the publish frequency, so a message can be logged at a
    higher rate than it is published to clients, or the other way around. Like the publish
    frequency it is shared by every client and stays in effect until the drone reboots, with
    one exception: on the X3 Ultra and X7 a multibeam recording raises the log rate of
    `PositionEstimateTel`, `AttitudeTel`, `CalibratedImuTel`, `CalibratedImuHpTel`,
    `DepthTel` and `AltitudeTel` while it runs and restores their defaults when it stops,
    which replaces a rate set here for those six.

    Args:
        msg (proto.message.Message): The message to set the log frequency of. Needs to be one
                                     of the messages in blueye.protocol that end in Tel, e.g.,
                                     blueye.protocol.Imu1Tel.
        frequency (float): The frequency in Hz. Must be greater than 0 and at most 100.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the frequency is not greater than 0 and at most 100 Hz.
        RuntimeError:
            If the connected drone is running a Blunux version older than 5.1.0, or if the
            drone refuses to change the log frequency, because the connected drone does not
            publish the message or logs it as its data arrives rather than on a timer.
    """
    self._parent_drone._verify_required_blunux_version("5.1.0")
    self._check_frequency(frequency)
    resp = self._parent_drone._req_rep_client.set_telemetry_msg_log_frequency(msg, frequency)
    if not resp.success:
        name = message_type_name(msg)
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"The drone could not change the log frequency of {name}. Either this drone does "
            "not publish it, or it is logged when its data arrives rather than on a timer"
        )

set_msg_publish_frequency(msg: Message, frequency: float)

Set the publishing frequency of a specific telemetry message.

The drone has one telemetry publisher shared by every connected client, so the new rate also applies to the Blueye app and any other SDK client, and it stays in effect until the drone reboots. Set the rate back before exiting if other clients depend on it.

Only messages the drone publishes on a timer have a publish frequency. The messages in EVENT_DRIVEN_TELEMETRY are published when their data arrives, and messages from peripherals are only published while the peripheral is connected.

Parameters:

  • msg (Message) –

    The message to set the frequency of. Needs to be one of the messages in blueye.protocol that end in Tel, e.g., blueye.protocol.DepthTel.

  • frequency (float) –

    The frequency in Hz. Must be greater than 0 and at most 100.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the frequency is not greater than 0 and at most 100 Hz.

  • RuntimeError –

    If the drone refuses to change the frequency, because the message is published when its data arrives rather than on a timer, or because the connected drone does not publish it.

def set_msg_publish_frequency(self, msg: proto.message.Message, frequency: float):
    """Set the publishing frequency of a specific telemetry message.

    The drone has one telemetry publisher shared by every connected client, so the new rate
    also applies to the Blueye app and any other SDK client, and it stays in effect until the
    drone reboots. Set the rate back before exiting if other clients depend on it.

    Only messages the drone publishes on a timer have a publish frequency. The messages in
    [`EVENT_DRIVEN_TELEMETRY`][blueye.sdk.constants.EVENT_DRIVEN_TELEMETRY] are published
    when their data arrives, and messages from peripherals are only published while the
    peripheral is connected.

    Args:
        msg (proto.message.Message): The message to set the frequency of. Needs to be one of the
                                     messages in blueye.protocol that end in Tel, e.g.,
                                     blueye.protocol.DepthTel.
        frequency (float): The frequency in Hz. Must be greater than 0 and at most 100.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the frequency is not greater than 0 and at most 100 Hz.
        RuntimeError:
            If the drone refuses to change the frequency, because the message is published
            when its data arrives rather than on a timer, or because the connected drone does
            not publish it.
    """
    self._check_frequency(frequency)
    resp = self._parent_drone._req_rep_client.set_telemetry_msg_publish_frequency(
        msg, frequency
    )
    if not resp.success:
        name = message_type_name(msg)
        if name in _EVENT_DRIVEN_TELEMETRY_NAMES:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"The drone publishes {name} when its data arrives, not on a timer, so its "
                "publish frequency cannot be changed"
            )
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"The drone could not change the publish frequency of {name}. Either it is not a "
            "telemetry message, or this drone does not publish it: messages from peripherals "
            "are only published while the peripheral is connected"
        )

def get_angle(self) -> Optional[float]:
    """Get the current position of the servo as an angle in degrees.

    Deprecated, the servo reports a position and not an angle. Use
    [`get_position`][blueye.sdk.guestport.GenericServo.get_position]. Position 0 maps to
    -90, 0.5 to 0 and 1 to 90.

    Returns:
        The angle (-90..90), or None if the drone has not reported the position.
    """
    warnings.warn(
        "`GenericServo.get_angle` is deprecated and will be removed in the next major "
        "version. Use `GenericServo.get_position()`, which returns the 0..1 position.",
        DeprecationWarning,
        stacklevel=2,
    )
    position = self.get_position()
    if position is None:
        return None
    return self.min_angle + position * (self.max_angle - self.min_angle)

def set_angle(self, angle: float) -> None:
    """Set the position of the servo from an angle in degrees.

    Deprecated, the servo takes a position and not an angle. Use
    [`set_position`][blueye.sdk.guestport.GenericServo.set_position]. -90 maps to 0, 0 to
    0.5 and 90 to 1, which is what the old degree calls drove the servo to.

    Args:
        angle (float): The angle (-90..90), mapped linearly onto the 0..1 position.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the angle is not within the allowed range.
    """
    warnings.warn(
        "`GenericServo.set_angle` is deprecated and will be removed in the next major "
        "version. Use `GenericServo.set_position()` with a 0..1 position instead.",
        DeprecationWarning,
        stacklevel=2,
    )
    if not self.min_angle <= angle <= self.max_angle:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Angle must be between {self.min_angle} and {self.max_angle} degrees."
        )
    self.set_position((angle - self.min_angle) / (self.max_angle - self.min_angle))

    self._grip_velocity = value

        self._grip_velocity, self._rotation_velocity
    )

configure(timeout: float = 0.5) -> _ParamsBatch

Return a context manager for batching camera parameter changes.

All attribute assignments on the returned object are accumulated and sent as a single set_camera_parameters request when the with block exits. If an exception is raised inside the block the changes are discarded.

Parameters take the same names and values as the corresponding setters; the protobuf field names and enums are accepted as well.

Parameters:

  • timeout (float, default: 0.5 ) –

    Timeout in seconds for the request. Increase when changing parameters that trigger pipeline restarts (e.g. codec, resolution).

Raises:

    If a value is not valid for the parameter being set.

  • RuntimeError –

    If a parameter requires a newer Blunux version than the drone runs.

Usage::

with drone.camera.configure() as params:
    params.recording_codec = bp.RecordingCodec.RECORDING_CODEC_H265
    params.recording_bitrate = 20_000_000
# sent here

def configure(self, timeout: float = 0.5) -> _ParamsBatch:
    """Return a context manager for batching camera parameter changes.

    All attribute assignments on the returned object are accumulated and sent as a single
    ``set_camera_parameters`` request when the ``with`` block exits.  If an exception is
    raised inside the block the changes are discarded.

    Parameters take the same names and values as the corresponding setters; the protobuf
    field names and enums are accepted as well.

    Args:
        timeout (float, optional): Timeout in seconds for the request. Increase when changing
            parameters that trigger pipeline restarts (e.g. codec, resolution).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a value is not valid for the parameter being set.
        RuntimeError: If a parameter requires a newer Blunux version than the drone runs.

    Usage::

        with drone.camera.configure() as params:
            params.recording_codec = bp.RecordingCodec.RECORDING_CODEC_H265
            params.recording_bitrate = 20_000_000
        # sent here
    """
    return self._ParamsBatch(self, timeout=timeout)

def enable_ehdr(self, enable_ehdr: bool):
    """Enable or disable the eHDR mode.

    Only available on the X3 Ultra and X7.

    Args:
        enable_ehdr (bool): True to enable eHDR mode, False to disable it. Enabled by default.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the connected drone is running a Blunux version older than 5.0.0.

    self._parent_drone._verify_required_blunux_version("5.0.0")
    if self._camera_parameters is None:
        self._update_camera_parameters()
    self._camera_parameters.ehdr_enabled = enable_ehdr
    self._parent_drone._req_rep_client.set_camera_parameters(self._camera_parameters)

Get the intrinsic calibration of the camera.

The X3 Ultra and X7 publish the main camera calibration (pinhole model with OpenCV distortion coefficients) in the DroneInfoTel telemetry message. The values are in pixels at the resolution the calibration was computed at, see get_scaled_calibration for a version matching the video resolution. is_default is set when the drone reports the model's built-in calibration rather than one measured for this particular drone.

Older models and the guestport camera do not publish a calibration.

def get_calibration(self) -> Optional[blueye.protocol.CameraCalibration]:
    """Get the intrinsic calibration of the camera.

    The X3 Ultra and X7 publish the main camera calibration (pinhole model with OpenCV
    distortion coefficients) in the `DroneInfoTel` telemetry message. The values are in
    pixels at the resolution the calibration was computed at, see
    [`get_scaled_calibration`][blueye.sdk.camera.Camera.get_scaled_calibration] for a version
    matching the video resolution. `is_default` is set when the drone reports the model's
    built-in calibration rather than one measured for this particular drone.

    Older models and the guestport camera do not publish a calibration.

    Returns:
        The camera calibration, or None if the drone has not published one.
    """
    if self._is_guestport_camera:
        return None
    drone_info = self._parent_drone.get_drone_info()
    if drone_info is None or drone_info.main_camera_calibration._pb.ByteSize() == 0:
        return None
    return drone_info.main_camera_calibration

def get_color_correction(self) -> Optional[blueye.protocol.FilterMessage]:
    """Get the color correction filter settings of the main camera.

    The color correction filter restores the red and blue balance that water absorbs with
    depth, driven by the depth and the scene. Only available on the X3 Ultra and X7.

    The drone publishes `ColorCorrectionTel` when the settings change rather than at a fixed
    rate. The value is the last change seen since connecting, and the drone is asked for its
    current settings if there has been none.

    Returns:
        The filter settings with `enabled` and `intensity` (0..1), or None if the drone has
        not reported any, as is the case for older models and the guestport camera.

def get_detach_status(self) -> bp.GuestPortDetachStatus:
    """Get the current attach state of a detachable device.

    The state is read from the latest drone info telemetry so it follows the device being
    attached or detached during a session. If no newer telemetry is available, the state
    reported when the peripheral was discovered is returned.

    Returns:
        The detach status. `GUEST_PORT_DETACH_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED` for devices that cannot be
        detached.
    """
    drone_info_tel = self.parent_drone.telemetry.get(bp.DroneInfoTel)
    if drone_info_tel is not None:
        device = _find_device(drone_info_tel.drone_info.gp, self)
        if device is not None:
            return device.detach_status
    return self._detach_status

Get the camera calibration scaled to a video resolution.

See scale_calibration for how the values are scaled.

Parameters:

  • resolution (Resolution | tuple[int, int], default: None ) –

    The resolution to scale the calibration to, either as a blueye.protocol.Resolution or as a (width, height) tuple in pixels. A Resolution maps to the frame size the drone's video pipeline produces for it: 640x480 for 480p and 16:9 for the others. Defaults to the current stream resolution.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the resolution is not a blueye.protocol.Resolution or a (width, height) tuple of positive integers.

  • RuntimeError –

    If the drone reports a stream resolution the SDK does not recognize.

Returns:

  • Optional[CameraCalibration] –

    The scaled calibration, or None if the drone has not published one.

Source code in blueye/sdk/camera.py 
def get_scaled_calibration(
    self,
    resolution: Union[blueye.protocol.Resolution, Tuple[int, int], None] = None,
) -> Optional[blueye.protocol.CameraCalibration]:
    """Get the camera calibration scaled to a video resolution.

    See [`scale_calibration`][blueye.sdk.camera.scale_calibration] for how the values are
    scaled.

    Args:
        resolution (blueye.protocol.Resolution | tuple[int, int], optional):
            The resolution to scale the calibration to, either as a
            `blueye.protocol.Resolution` or as a `(width, height)` tuple in pixels. A
            `Resolution` maps to the frame size the drone's video pipeline produces for it:
            640x480 for 480p and 16:9 for the others. Defaults to the current stream
            resolution.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the resolution is not a `blueye.protocol.Resolution` or a
            `(width, height)` tuple of positive integers.
        RuntimeError: If the drone reports a stream resolution the SDK does not recognize.

    Returns:
        The scaled calibration, or None if the drone has not published one.
    """
    calibration = self.get_calibration()
    if calibration is None:
        return None
    if resolution is None:
        resolution = self.get_stream_resolution()
    if isinstance(resolution, blueye.protocol.Resolution):
        try:
            width, height = _RESOLUTION_TO_SIZE[resolution]
        except KeyError:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Drone reported an unsupported resolution: {describe_enum(resolution)}"
            ) from None
    else:
        try:
            width, height = resolution
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{resolution!r} is not a valid resolution, expected a "
                "blueye.protocol.Resolution or a (width, height) tuple"
            ) from None
    return scale_calibration(calibration, width, height)

get_turbidity_filter() -> Optional[FilterMessage]

Get the turbidity filter settings of the main camera.

The turbidity filter runs contrast limited adaptive histogram equalisation (CLAHE) on the video, which brings out detail in turbid water. Only available on the X3 Ultra and X7.

The drone publishes TurbidityFilterTel when the settings change rather than at a fixed rate. The value is the last change seen since connecting, and the drone is asked for its current settings if there has been none.

    The filter settings with enabled and intensity (0..1), or None if the drone has not reported any, as is the case for older models and the guestport camera.

def get_turbidity_filter(self) -> Optional[blueye.protocol.FilterMessage]:
    """Get the turbidity filter settings of the main camera.

    The turbidity filter runs contrast limited adaptive histogram equalisation (CLAHE) on
    the video, which brings out detail in turbid water. Only available on the X3 Ultra and
    X7.

    The drone publishes `TurbidityFilterTel` when the settings change rather than at a fixed
    rate. The value is the last change seen since connecting, and the drone is asked for its
    current settings if there has been none.

    Returns:
        The filter settings with `enabled` and `intensity` (0..1), or None if the drone has
        not reported any, as is the case for older models and the guestport camera.
    """
    if self._is_guestport_camera:
        return None
    tel = self._parent_drone.telemetry.get(blueye.protocol.TurbidityFilterTel)
    if tel is None:
        return None
    return tel.turbidity_filter

set_pan_tilt_zoom(
    pan: Optional[float] = None,
    tilt: Optional[float] = None,
    zoom: Optional[float] = None,
)

Set the digital pan, tilt and zoom of the main camera.

The three values are sent together in one message. An argument that is left out keeps the value this object last sent. Before the first call it keeps the value the drone last reported, or 0 if it has not reported one. The drone reports a change about 0.1 s after the command, which is why the last sent values are used rather than the report: two calls in a row would otherwise undo each other. A change made by another client after the last call from this object is not picked up; pass all three values to be sure. Pan and tilt only have an effect while zoomed in, since at zoom 0 the whole sensor image is already shown.

Laser dot tracking works on the full, unzoomed image, so enable_tracking resets pan, tilt and zoom to 0 when it starts, as the Blueye app does.

Parameters:

  • pan (float, default: None ) –

    Horizontal pan (-1..1), 0 is centred.

  • tilt (float, default: None ) –

    Vertical tilt (-1..1), 0 is centred.

  • zoom (float, default: None ) –

    Zoom level (0..1), 0 is no zoom.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If pan or tilt is outside -1..1, or zoom is outside 0..1.

  • RuntimeError –

    If this is the guestport camera, the drone runs Blunux older than 5.0.0, or the drone is neither an X3 Ultra nor an X7.

Source code in blueye/sdk/camera.py 
def set_pan_tilt_zoom(
    self,
    pan: Optional[float] = None,
    tilt: Optional[float] = None,
    zoom: Optional[float] = None,
):
    """Set the digital pan, tilt and zoom of the main camera.

    The three values are sent together in one message. An argument that is left out keeps
    the value this object last sent. Before the first call it keeps the value the drone last
    reported, or 0 if it has not reported one. The drone reports a change about 0.1 s after
    the command, which is why the last sent values are used rather than the report: two
    calls in a row would otherwise undo each other. A change made by another client after
    the last call from this object is not picked up; pass all three values to be sure. Pan
    and tilt only have an effect while zoomed in, since at zoom 0 the whole sensor image is
    already shown.

    Laser dot tracking works on the full, unzoomed image, so
    [`enable_tracking`][blueye.sdk.guestport.Laser.enable_tracking] resets pan, tilt and
    zoom to 0 when it starts, as the Blueye app does.

    Args:
        pan (float, optional): Horizontal pan (-1..1), 0 is centred.
        tilt (float, optional): Vertical tilt (-1..1), 0 is centred.
        zoom (float, optional): Zoom level (0..1), 0 is no zoom.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If pan or tilt is outside -1..1, or zoom is outside 0..1.
        RuntimeError: If this is the guestport camera, the drone runs Blunux older than
            5.0.0, or the drone is neither an X3 Ultra nor an X7.
    """
    self._verify_4k_camera("Digital pan, tilt and zoom")
    if pan is not None:
        self._verify_in_range("Pan", pan, -1.0, 1.0)
    if tilt is not None:
        self._verify_in_range("Tilt", tilt, -1.0, 1.0)
    if zoom is not None:
        self._verify_in_range("Zoom", zoom, 0.0, 1.0)
    if None in (pan, tilt, zoom):
        if self._last_pan_tilt_zoom is not None:
            current = self._last_pan_tilt_zoom
        else:
            reported = self.get_pan_tilt_zoom()
            current = (
                (reported.pan, reported.tilt, reported.zoom)
                if reported is not None
                else (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            )
        pan = current[0] if pan is None else pan
        tilt = current[1] if tilt is None else tilt
        zoom = current[2] if zoom is None else zoom
    self._send_pan_tilt_zoom(pan, tilt, zoom)

def set_recording(self, start_recording: bool):
    """Set the camera recording state.

    Args:
        start_recording (bool): Set to True to start a recording, set to False to stop the
                                current recording.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If a recording is started while the drone's storage settings have
            videos switched off, in which case the drone would not record.
    """
    if start_recording and self._parent_drone._media_is_enabled("videos") is False:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "The drone's storage settings have video recording switched off, so it would not "
            "record. Enable videos under the drone's storage settings in the Blueye app."
        )
    record_state = self._get_record_state()
    if record_state is None:
        logger.warning("Unable to set recording state, no record state telemetry received")
        return
    # The drone applies all three recorders from one message, so the other camera and the
    # multibeam are sent as they are, from the latest RecordStateTel
    if self._is_guestport_camera:
        self._parent_drone._ctrl_client.set_recording_state(
            record_state.main_is_recording,
            start_recording,
            record_state.multibeam_is_recording,
        )
    else:
        self._parent_drone._ctrl_client.set_recording_state(
            start_recording,
            record_state.guestport_is_recording,
            record_state.multibeam_is_recording,
        )

def set_resolution(self, resolution: int):
    """Set the camera resolution.

    Deprecated:
        Drones running Blunux 4.4 or newer ignore this field when camera parameters are set,
        so calling this method has no effect on them. Use
        [`set_stream_resolution`][blueye.sdk.camera.Camera.set_stream_resolution] and

            1440 or 2160.

def get_detach_status(self) -> bp.GuestPortDetachStatus:
    """Get the current attach state of a detachable device.

    The state is read from the latest drone info telemetry so it follows the device being
    attached or detached during a session. If no newer telemetry is available, the state
    reported when the peripheral was discovered is returned.

    Returns:
        The detach status. `GUEST_PORT_DETACH_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED` for devices that cannot be
        detached.
    """
    drone_info_tel = self.parent_drone.telemetry.get(bp.DroneInfoTel)
    if drone_info_tel is not None:
        device = _find_device(drone_info_tel.drone_info.gp, self)
        if device is not None:
            return device.detach_status
    return self._detach_status

def get_intensity(self) -> Optional[float]:

    in the session, so this can be `None` for a while after connecting.

enable_tracking(enabled: bool)

Start or stop laser dot tracking.

Tracking modulates the laser at 5 Hz, and the drone picks the flickering dots out of the main camera image. Only available on the X3 Ultra and X7; older firmware ignores the flag. The intensity stays as the drone last reported it, or as last commanded from this object in the last two seconds or while the drone has not reported any, and a laser that is off is turned fully on when tracking starts, since the drone needs the dots to track. Tracking works on the full camera image, so starting it also resets the digital pan, tilt and zoom to 0, as the Blueye app does.

Parameters:

  • enabled (bool) –

    True to start tracking, False to stop it and keep the laser on continuously.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError –

    If the drone is known to be neither an X3 Ultra nor an X7.

Source code in blueye/sdk/guestport.py 
def enable_tracking(self, enabled: bool):
    """Start or stop laser dot tracking.

    Tracking modulates the laser at 5 Hz, and the drone picks the flickering dots out of the
    main camera image. Only available on the X3 Ultra and X7; older firmware ignores the
    flag. The intensity stays as the drone last reported it, or as last commanded from this
    object in the last two seconds or while the drone has not reported any, and a laser
    that is off is turned fully on when tracking starts, since the drone needs the dots to
    track. Tracking works on the full camera image, so starting it also resets the digital
    pan, tilt and zoom to 0, as the Blueye app does.

    Args:
        enabled (bool): True to start tracking, False to stop it and keep the laser on
            continuously.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the drone is known to be neither an X3 Ultra nor an X7.
    """
    if self.parent_drone.is_jetson_platform() is False:
        raise RuntimeError("Laser tracking is only available on the X3 Ultra and X7")
    intensity = self.get_intensity()
    if intensity is None or self._is_fresh(self._intensity_commanded_at):
        intensity = self._commanded_intensity
    if enabled and not intensity:
        intensity = 1.0
    elif intensity is None:
        intensity = 0.0
    if enabled:
        # Through the camera, so its record of the last sent values stays right
        self.parent_drone.camera._send_pan_tilt_zoom(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    self._send(intensity, enabled, modulation_explicit=True)

For two seconds after the flag was chosen from this object, with this argument or with enable_tracking, that choice is kept instead, since the drone reports the laser once a second and the report may predate it. def set_intensity(self, intensity: float, modulated: Optional[bool] = None):
    """Set the intensity of the laser.

    If the laser does not support dimming but only on and off, a value of 0 turns the laser off,
    and any value above 0 turns the laser on.

    Args:
        intensity (float): The intensity of the laser (0..1).
        modulated (bool, optional): Whether the laser is modulated for dot tracking. Left out,
            the setting the drone last reported is kept, so an intensity change does not
            switch tracking off. For two seconds after the flag was chosen from this object,
            with this argument or with `enable_tracking`, that choice is kept instead, since
            the drone reports the laser once a second and the report may predate it. A call
            that leaves the flag out does not restart those two seconds, so a script that
            sets the intensity often still follows what another client does to tracking. See
            [`enable_tracking`][blueye.sdk.guestport.Laser.enable_tracking].

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the intensity is not between 0 and 1.
    """
    if not 0 <= intensity <= 1:
        raise ValueError("Laser intensity must be between 0 and 1.")
    explicit = modulated is not None
    if modulated is None:
        laser = self._get_laser()
        if self._is_fresh(self._modulation_commanded_at) or laser is None:
            modulated = self._commanded_modulated
        else:
            modulated = laser.modulated
    self._send(intensity, modulated, modulation_explicit=explicit)

def __init__(
    self, parent_drone: "Drone", port_number: bp.GuestPortNumber, device: bp.GuestPortDevice
):
    """Initialize the Peripheral class.

    Args:
        parent_drone (Drone): The parent drone instance.
        port_number (bp.GuestPortNumber): The guest port number.
        device (bp.GuestPortDevice): The guest port device.
    """
    self.parent_drone = parent_drone
    self.port_number: bp.GuestPortNumber = port_number
    self.name: str = device.name
    self.manufacturer: str = device.manufacturer
    self.serial_number: str = device.serial_number
    self.depth_rating: float = device.depth_rating
    self.required_blunux_version: str = device.required_blunux_version
    self.device_id: bp.GuestPortDeviceID = device.device_id
    self._detach_status: bp.GuestPortDetachStatus = device.detach_status
    self.required_capabilities: List[bp.GuestPortCapability] = list(
        device.required_capabilities
    )
    """Interfaces the device requires from the port it is connected to."""
    self.compatible_guest_ports: List[bp.GuestPortNumber] = list(device.compatible_guest_ports)
    """Ports on this drone where the device is fully supported.

    Computed by the drone from the port capabilities and the device requirements."""
    if self.required_blunux_version != "":
        if version.parse(self.required_blunux_version) > version.parse(
            parent_drone.software_version_short
        ):
            logger.warning(
                f"Peripheral {self.name} requires Blunux version "
                f"{self.required_blunux_version}, but the drone is running "
                f"{parent_drone.software_version_short}"
            )

def connector_info_to_guest_port(
    parent_drone: "Drone", connector_info: bp.GuestPortConnectorInfo
) -> GuestPort:
    """Build a [GuestPort][blueye.sdk.guestport.GuestPort] from the drone's connector info.

    Args:
        parent_drone (Drone): The parent drone instance.
        connector_info (bp.GuestPortConnectorInfo): The per-port message from `GuestPortInfo`.

    Returns:
        The guest port with its capabilities, connector error, and discovered peripherals.
    """
    port = GuestPort(
        number=connector_info.guest_port_number,
        capabilities=list(connector_info.capabilities),
    )
    if "error" in connector_info:
        port.error = connector_info.error
        if port.error == bp.GuestPortError.GUEST_PORT_ERROR_NOT_CONNECTED:
            logger.debug(f"Nothing connected to {describe_enum(port.number)}")
        else:
            logger.warning(
                f"Guest port {describe_enum(port.number)} reports connector error "
                f"{describe_enum(port.error)}"
            )
    else:
        for device in connector_info.device_list.devices:
            port.devices.append(device_to_peripheral(parent_drone, port.number, device))
    return port

def device_to_peripheral(
    parent_drone: "Drone", port_number: bp.GuestPortNumber, device: bp.GuestPortDevice
) -> Peripheral:
    """Convert a device to its corresponding peripheral class.

    Args:
        parent_drone (Drone): The parent drone instance.
        port_number (bp.GuestPortNumber): The guest port number.
        device (bp.GuestPortDevice): The guest port device.

    Returns:
        The corresponding peripheral class instance.
    """
    logger.debug(f"Found a {device.name} at port {port_number}")
    if device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_BLUEYE_CAM:
        peripheral = GuestPortCamera(parent_drone, port_number, device)
    elif (
        device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_BLUEYE_LIGHT
        or device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_BLUEYE_LIGHT_PAIR
        or device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_BLUE_ROBOTICS_LUMEN
    ):
        peripheral = GuestPortLight(parent_drone, port_number, device)
    elif (
        device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_BLUE_ROBOTICS_NEWTON
        or device.device_id
        == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_BLUE_ROBOTICS_DETACHABLE_NEWTON
        or device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_BLUEPRINT_LAB_REACH_ALPHA
    ):
        peripheral = Gripper(parent_drone, port_number, device)
    elif (
        device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_BLUEYE_SCALING_LASER
        or device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_LASER_TOOLS_SEA_BEAM
        or device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_SPOT_X_LASER_SCALERS
    ):
        peripheral = Laser(parent_drone, port_number, device)
    elif device.device_id == bp.GuestPortDeviceID.GUEST_PORT_DEVICE_ID_BLUEYE_GENERIC_SERVO:
        peripheral = GenericServo(parent_drone, port_number, device)
    elif device.device_id in SkidServo._ANGLE_LIMITS:
        peripheral = SkidServo(parent_drone, port_number, device)
    else:
        peripheral = Peripheral(parent_drone, port_number, device)
    return peripheral

Download the specified log to your local file system

If you specify an output_path the log file will be downloaded to that directory instead of the current one.

Specifying output_name will overwrite the default file name with whatever you have specified (be sure to include the .csv extension).

The drone samples the log content at 10 Hz, and by default this function downsamples this rate to 1 Hz.

Source code in blueye/sdk/logs.py 
def download(
    self, output_path=None, output_name=None, downsample_divisor=10, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT
):
    """
    Download the specified log to your local file system

    If you specify an output_path the log file will be downloaded to that directory
    instead of the current one.

    Specifying output_name will overwrite the default file name with whatever you
    have specified (be sure to include the .csv extension).

    The drone samples the log content at 10 Hz, and by default this function downsamples this
    rate to 1 Hz.

    `timeout` is the seconds to wait for the drone to connect and then between bytes.
    Raises `requests.HTTPError` if the drone answers with an error status.
    """
    response = requests.get(
        self.download_path, params={"divisor": downsample_divisor}, timeout=timeout
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    log = response.content
    if output_path is None:
        output_path = "./"
    if output_name is None:
        output_name = self.name
    with open(f"{output_path}{output_name}", "wb") as f:
        f.write(log)

Download a log file from the drone

Arguments:

  • output_path: Path to write the log file to. If None, the log will be written to the current working directory. If the path is a directory, the log will be downloaded to that directory with its original name. Else the log will be downloaded to the specified path.
  • write_to_file: If True, the log will be written to the specified path. If False, the log will only be returned as a bytes object.
  • timeout: Seconds to wait for the drone to connect, and then between bytes of the response. This is the requests timeout, so it does not limit the total download time.
  • overwrite_cache: If True, the log will be downloaded even if it is already been downloaded. Open logs (is_open) are always downloaded again, since the drone is still writing to them.

Returns:

The compressed log file as a bytes object.

Raises:

requests.HTTPError if the drone answers with an error status, and requests.ConnectionError or requests.Timeout if it does not answer.

Source code in blueye/sdk/logs.py 
def download(
    self,
    output_path: Optional[Path | str] = None,
    write_to_file: bool = True,
    timeout: float = 1,
    overwrite_cache: bool = False,
) -> bytes:
    """Download a log file from the drone

    *Arguments*:

    * `output_path`:
        Path to write the log file to. If `None`, the log will be written to the
        current working directory. If the path is a directory, the log will be
        downloaded to that directory with its original name. Else the log will be
        downloaded to the specified path.
    * `write_to_file`:
        If True, the log will be written to the specified path. If False, the
        log will only be returned as a bytes object.
    * `timeout`:
        Seconds to wait for the drone to connect, and then between bytes of the response.
        This is the `requests` timeout, so it does not limit the total download time.
    * `overwrite_cache`:
        If True, the log will be downloaded even if it is already been downloaded.
        Open logs (`is_open`) are always downloaded again, since the drone is still
        writing to them.

    *Returns*:

    The compressed log file as a bytes object.

    *Raises*:

    `requests.HTTPError` if the drone answers with an error status, and
    `requests.ConnectionError` or `requests.Timeout` if it does not answer.
    """
    if self.is_open:
        logger.warning(
            f"Log {self.name} is still being written by the drone, so the download is a "
            "snapshot that stops mid-record"
        )
    if self.content is None or overwrite_cache or self.is_open:
        response = requests.get(self.download_url, timeout=timeout)
        response.raise_for_status()
        self.content = response.content
    if write_to_file:
        if output_path is None:
            output_path = Path(f"{self.name}.bez")
        else:
            if type(output_path) == str:
                output_path = Path(output_path)
            if output_path.is_dir():
                output_path = output_path.joinpath(f"{self.name}.bez")
        with open(output_path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(self.content)
    return self.content

    decompress: bool = True,

Class for streaming a log

Creates a stream from a downloaded log file. Iterate over the object to get the next log record as a tuple of

  • the wall clock time of the record (DatetimeWithNanoseconds, UTC),
  • the time since the first record in the log (timedelta),
  • the message type, eg. bp.DepthTel, and
  • the message itself.

A log can hold types this SDK does not know, for instance when the drone runs a newer release than the installed blueye.protocol package. By default those records are skipped: the first one of each type logs a warning, and all of them are counted per type URL in unknown_types. Pass include_unknown=True to get them as (time, time since first record, type URL, raw payload bytes) tuples instead, where the type URL is a string such as "type.googleapis.com/blueye.protocol.PowerCanisterTel".

Source code in blueye/sdk/logs.py 
def __init__(
    self, log: bytes, decompress: bool = True, include_unknown: bool = False
) -> Iterator[
    Tuple[
        proto.datetime_helpers.DatetimeWithNanoseconds,  # Real time clock
        timedelta,  # Time since first message
        Union[type, str],  # Message type, or its type URL if the SDK does not know it
        Union[proto.message.Message, bytes],  # Message contents, or the raw payload
    ]
]:
    if decompress:
        self.stream = StreamingDecompressor(log)
    else:
        self.stream = io.BytesIO(log)

    self.include_unknown = include_unknown
    #: Type URL -> number of records in the stream so far that could not be decoded
    self.unknown_types: Dict[str, int] = {}
    self.start_monotonic: proto.datetime_helpers.DatetimeWithNanoseconds = 0
    self._summary_logged = False

def filter(self, filter_func: Callable[[LogFile], bool]) -> Logs:
    """Return a new Logs object with only those matching the filter

    Eg. to get logs classified as a dive:
    ```
    dive_logs = myDrone.logs.filter(lambda log: log.is_dive)
    ```

    or to get all logs with a max depth greater than 10m:
    ```
    deep_logs = myDrone.logs.filter(lambda log: log.max_depth_magnitude > 10)
    ```
    """
    if not self.index_downloaded:
        self.refresh_log_index()
    filtered_logs = Logs(self._parent_drone)
    filtered_logs.index_downloaded = True
    for log in self:
        if filter_func(log):
            filtered_logs._logs[log.name] = log
    return filtered_logs

Refresh the log index from the drone

This is method is run on the first log access by default, but if you would like to check for new log files it can be called at any time.

def refresh_log_index(self, timeout: float = HTTP_TIMEOUT):
    """Refresh the log index from the drone

    This is method is run on the first log access by default, but if you would like to check
    for new log files it can be called at any time.

    `timeout` is the seconds to wait for each request to the drone. Raises
    `requests.HTTPError` if the drone answers with an error status.
    """
    if not self._parent_drone.connected:
        raise ConnectionError(
            "The connection to the drone is not established, try calling the connect method "
            "before retrying"
        )
    logger.debug("Refreshing log index")
    logs_endpoint = f"http://{self._parent_drone._ip}/logs"
    response = requests.get(logs_endpoint, timeout=timeout)
    response.raise_for_status()
    logs: List[dict] = response.json()

    if version.parse(self._parent_drone.software_version_short) < version.parse("3.3"):
        # Extend index with dive info, sends a request for each log file so can be quite slow
        # for drones with many logs. Not necessary for Blunux >= 3.3 as dive info is included in
        # the index.
        logger.debug(f"Getting dive info for {len(logs)} logs")
        for index, log in enumerate(logs):
            response = requests.get(f"{logs_endpoint}/{log['name']}/dive_info", timeout=timeout)
            response.raise_for_status()
            logs[index].update(response.json())

    # Instantiate log objects for each log
    logger.debug(f"Creating log objects for {len(logs)} logs")
    for log in logs:
        if log["has_binlog"]:
            self._logs[log["name"]] = LogFile(
                log["name"],
                log["is_dive"],
                log["binlog_size"],
                log["start_time"],
                log["max_depth_magnitude"],
                self._parent_drone._ip,
                is_open=log.get("is_open", False),
            )
        else:
            logger.info(f"Log {log['name']} does not have a binlog, ignoring")
    self.index_downloaded = True

def __init__(self, compressed_data: bytes):
    self.compressed_data = compressed_data
    self.compressed_pos = 0
    self.decompressor = None
    self.decompressed_buffer = bytearray()
    self.eof = False

    if is_gzip_compressed(compressed_data):
        # Initialize zlib decompressor for gzip data
        self.decompressor = zlib.decompressobj(wbits=zlib.MAX_WBITS | 16)
    else:
        # Data is not compressed
        self.decompressed_buffer = bytearray(compressed_data)
        self.eof = True

Read up to size bytes from the decompressed stream

Source code in blueye/sdk/logs.py 
def read(self, size: int) -> bytes:
    """Read up to size bytes from the decompressed stream"""
    if self.eof and len(self.decompressed_buffer) == 0:
        return b""

    # If we need more decompressed data and we're not at EOF
    while len(self.decompressed_buffer) < size and not self.eof:
        # Read a chunk from compressed data
        chunk_size = min(8192, len(self.compressed_data) - self.compressed_pos)
        if chunk_size == 0:
            # No more compressed data
            if self.decompressor:
                # Finalize decompression. This can fail on corrupted data.
                try:
                    final_data = self.decompressor.flush()
                    self.decompressed_buffer.extend(final_data)
                except zlib.error as e:
                    logger.warning(
                        f"Decompression flush failed, likely due to corrupted data: {e}"
                    )
                except (MemoryError, OverflowError) as e:
                    logger.error(f"Decompression flush failed due to resource limits: {e}")
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.error(f"Unexpected error during decompression flush: {e}")
            self.eof = True
            break

        chunk = self.compressed_data[self.compressed_pos : self.compressed_pos + chunk_size]
        self.compressed_pos += chunk_size

        if self.decompressor:
            try:
                decompressed_chunk = self.decompressor.decompress(chunk)
                self.decompressed_buffer.extend(decompressed_chunk)
            except zlib.error as e:
                # If decompression fails, we're probably done. This can happen with
                # truncated or corrupted files.
                logger.warning(f"Decompression of chunk failed: {e}")
                self.eof = True
                break
            except (MemoryError, OverflowError) as e:
                logger.error(f"Decompression failed due to resource limits: {e}")
                self.eof = True
                break
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Unexpected error during decompression: {e}")
                self.eof = True
                break

    # Return requested amount of data
    result_size = min(size, len(self.decompressed_buffer))
    result = bytes(self.decompressed_buffer[:result_size])
    self.decompressed_buffer = self.decompressed_buffer[result_size:]

    return result

def human_readable_filesize(binsize: int) -> str:
    """Convert bytes to human readable string"""
    suffix = "B"
    num = binsize
    for unit in ["", "Ki", "Mi"]:
        if abs(num) < 1024.0:
            return f"{num:3.1f} {unit}{suffix}"
        num /= 1024.0
    return f"{num:.1f} Gi{suffix}"

def is_gzip_compressed(data: bytes) -> bool:
    """Check if data is gzip compressed by looking at the magic header bytes"""
    return len(data) >= 2 and data[0] == 0x1F and data[1] == 0x8B

    Args:
        mission: The mission to load and run.
        timeout: Seconds to wait for each step: for a mission status to arrive, for the drone to
            clear a previous mission, and for the new mission to become ready.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the connected drone does not meet the required Blunux version, or the
            drone fails to load the mission.
        TimeoutError: If no mission status arrives, or the mission does not become inactive or
            ready, within the timeout.
    """
    self._parent_drone._verify_required_blunux_version("4.0.5")

    # Wait for a status to know whether a previous mission has to be cleared first
    state = self._wait_for_state(None, timeout, "known")
    if state not in (
        bp.MissionState.MISSION_STATE_INACTIVE,
        bp.MissionState.MISSION_STATE_COMPLETED,
    ):
        self.clear()
        self._wait_for_state((bp.MissionState.MISSION_STATE_INACTIVE,), timeout, "inactive")

    self.send_new(mission)
    self._wait_for_state(
        (bp.MissionState.MISSION_STATE_READY,), timeout, "ready", load_failure_is_error=True
    )
    self.run()

def create_waypoint_instruction(
    waypoint_name: str,
    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,
    depth: float,
    speed_to_target: float = 0.6,
    speed_to_depth: float = 0.3,
    circle_of_acceptance: float = 1,
    waypoint_id: int = 0,
) -> bp.Instruction:
    """
    Helper function to create waypoint instructions.

    Args:
        waypoint_name (str): The name of the waypoint.
        latitude (float): The latitude of the waypoint (WGS 84 decimal format). Needs to be in the
                          range [-90, 90].
        longitude (float): The longitude of the waypoint (WGS 84 decimal format). Needs to be in the
                           range [-180, 180].
        depth (float): The depth of the waypoint (meters below surface).
        circle_of_acceptance: The radius of the circle of acceptance (meters).
        speed_to_target: The speed to the waypoint (m/s).
        waypoint_id: The ID of the waypoint.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If latitude or longitude are out of bounds.

    Returns:
        Instruction: An Instruction object with the specified waypoint details.
    """
    if not (-90 <= latitude <= 90):
        raise ValueError(f"Latitude must be between -90 and 90 degrees, got {latitude}")
    if not (-180 <= longitude <= 180):
        raise ValueError(f"Longitude must be between -180 and 180 degrees, got {longitude}")
    global_position = bp.LatLongPosition()
    global_position.latitude = latitude
    global_position.longitude = longitude

    depth_set_point = bp.DepthSetPoint()
    depth_set_point.depth = depth
    depth_set_point.depth_zero_reference = bp.DepthZeroReference.DEPTH_ZERO_REFERENCE_SURFACE
    depth_set_point.speed_to_depth = speed_to_depth

    waypoint = bp.Waypoint()
    waypoint.id = waypoint_id
    waypoint.name = waypoint_name
    waypoint.global_position = global_position
    waypoint.circle_of_acceptance = circle_of_acceptance
    waypoint.speed_to_target = speed_to_target
    waypoint.depth_set_point = depth_set_point

    waypoint_command = bp.WaypointCommand(waypoint=waypoint)

    instruction = bp.Instruction({"waypoint_command": waypoint_command})
    return instruction

def export_to_json(mission: bp.Mission, output_path: Optional[Path | str] = None):
    """Export the mission to a JSON file

    This allows you to save the mission to a file for later use or to share it with others.

    Args:
        mission: The mission to export
        output_path: The path to write the JSON file to. If `None` the mission will be written to
                     the current directory with the name `BlueyeMission.json`. If the path is a
                     directory, the mission will be written to that directory with the name
                     `BlueyeMission.json`. Else the mission will be written to the specified file.
    """
    if output_path is None:
        output_path = Path("BlueyeMission.json")
    else:
        if type(output_path) == str:
            output_path = Path(output_path)
        if output_path.is_dir():
            output_path = output_path.joinpath("BlueyeMission.json")

    logger.debug(f'Exporting mission "{mission.name}" to {output_path}')
    with open(output_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(MessageToJson(mission._pb))

Creates a mission from a list of instructions

The instructions are copied and numbered 1 to n in list order, which is the numbering the Blueye app uses. The drone executes the instructions in list order and reports progress by these ids: MissionStatus.completed_instruction_ids and ReferenceAutoPilot.active_instruction_id refer to them. The instructions passed in are left unchanged, so the same instruction object can appear more than once in the list.

Parameters:

    ID of the mission

  • mission_name (str, default: '' ) –

    Name of the mission

  • instruction_list (List[Instruction]) –

    List of instructions to create the mission from

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the number of instructions exceeds 50, which is the maximum allowed.

Returns:

  • Mission –

    A mission object with the instructions and their respective IDs

def prepare_new_mission(
    instruction_list: List[bp.Instruction],
    mission_id: int = 0,
    mission_name: str = "",
) -> bp.Mission:
    """Creates a mission from a list of instructions

    The instructions are copied and numbered 1 to n in list order, which is the numbering the
    Blueye app uses. The drone executes the instructions in list order and reports progress by
    these ids: `MissionStatus.completed_instruction_ids` and
    `ReferenceAutoPilot.active_instruction_id` refer to them. The instructions passed in are left
    unchanged, so the same instruction object can appear more than once in the list.

    Args:
        mission_id: ID of the mission
        mission_name: Name of the mission
        instruction_list: List of instructions to create the mission from

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the number of instructions exceeds 50, which is the maximum allowed.

    Returns:
        A mission object with the instructions and their respective IDs
    """
    if len(instruction_list) > 50:
        raise ValueError(
            "A mission can only contain up to 50 instructions. "
            f"Received {len(instruction_list)} instructions."
        )
    logger.debug(
        f'Preparing the "{mission_name}" mission, with ID {mission_id} and '
        f"{len(instruction_list)} instructions"
    )

    # Copy the instructions so the caller's objects keep their ids. Number from 1: the drone
    # reports progress by id, and 0 is also what an unset id reads back as.
    instructions = []
    for position, instruction in enumerate(instruction_list, start=1):
        instruction_copy = copy.deepcopy(instruction)
        instruction_copy.id = position
        instructions.append(instruction_copy)
    return bp.Mission(id=mission_id, name=mission_name, instructions=instructions)

Motion(parent_drone)

Control the motion of the drone, and set automatic control modes.

Motion can be set one degree of freedom at a time by using the motion setters (set_surge, set_sway, set_heave and set_yaw, and on the Blueye X7 also set_roll and set_pitch) or for all degrees of freedom in one go through the send_thruster_setpoint method.

A setpoint of 1 or -1 is full stick, not the most the thrusters can give. The force it asks for depends on set_boost and set_slow; see Control from a Python script for the levels per axis. The drone holds the last setpoint until it gets a new one, or until it zeroes the input 3 seconds after the client in control stops sending its watchdog.

Only the Blueye X7 has thrusters that can produce roll and pitch moments. The other models ignore roll and pitch input, so the setters are safe to call on any drone.

enable_auto_altitude(enable: bool)

Enable or disable the auto altitude control mode

When auto altitude is active, the drone will attempt to maintain its current altitude above the seabed. Heave input (set_heave or send_thruster_setpoint) specifies a speed set point instead of a force set point. A control loop on the drone will then attempt to maintain the wanted speed in the heave direction as long as auto altitude is active.

Auto altitude needs a valid altitude, which comes from a DVL or a downward-facing Ping sonar on a guest port. get_altitude() returns None while there is none. Without it the drone drops the request and only logs it on its own side, so check is_auto_altitude_active() afterwards. Enabling auto altitude turns auto depth off, also when the auto altitude request itself is dropped. If the altitude becomes invalid while auto altitude is active, the drone switches to auto depth.

Parameters:

  • enable (bool) –

    Activate auto altitude mode if true, de-activate if false.
